q: 1. The moment of inertia of a rectangular section 3 cm wide and 4 cm deep about X-X axis is
2. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load W. The maximum bending moment M is
explain: For a SS beam with total UDL 'W' (where W = w * L), the maximum bending moment at the center is WL/8 (or wL²/8).

q: 3. The maximum deflection of a fixed beam of length l carrying a central point load W is
explain: The deflection of a fixed beam is 1/4th of the deflection of a simply supported beam of the same span and load. Since SS beam deflection is Wl³/48EI, fixed beam deflection is Wl³/192EI.

q: 4. A concentrated load is one which
options: acts at a point on a beam
spreads non-uniformly over the whole length
spreads uniformly over the whole length
varies uniformly over the whole length
explain: A concentrated or point load is assumed to act at a single specific point on the beam's axis.

q: 5. The bending moment of a cantilever beam... carrying a gradually varying load from zero at free end and w per unit length at the fixed end is... at the fixed end.
explain: Total load wl/2 acts at a distance of l/3 from the base (fixed end). Moment = (wl/2) * (l/3) = wl²/6.

q: 6. The maximum bending moment of a simply supported beam of span l and carrying a point load w at the centre of beam, is
explain: Reaction at each support is w/2. Maximum BM at the center = (w/2) * (l/2) = wl/4.

q: 7. A beam is said to be in general, stable and statically determinate for general loading when the number of reaction components is
explain: In 2D space, there are 3 equations of equilibrium (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣM). A structure with 3 independent reaction components is statically determinate.

q: 8. A uniform girder simply supported at its ends... propped at the centre so as to neutralize the deflection. The net B.M. at the centre will be
explain: With a prop reaction of 5/8W, the net BM at the center becomes (WL/8) - (5/8W * L/4) = WL/32.

q: 9. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation?
explain: A free end has no constraints; it can move horizontally, vertically, and rotate freely under load.

q: 10. If Z and I are the section modulus and moment of inertia of the section, the shear force F and bending moment M at a section are related by
explain: The fundamental differential relationship between bending moment and shear force is that F (or V) is the derivative of M with respect to distance x.

q: 11. The shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is always
explain: UDL (constant) leads to a linear SFD, which integrates into a 2nd-degree parabolic curve for the BMD.

q: 12. The shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load, is always
explain: A uniformly increasing load (1st degree) leads to a parabolic SFD (2nd degree) and a cubical parabolic BMD (3rd degree).

q: 13. For a simply supported beam with a central load, the bending moment is
explain: For a simply supported beam of length L with a central point load P, the bending moment increases linearly from zero at the supports to a maximum value of PL/4 at the center.

q: 14. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load W over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
explain: In a cantilever beam with a UDL, the maximum bending moment occurs at the fixed support and is calculated as (Total Load × Distance to CG), which is W × (L/2) = WL/2.

q: 15. If the beam is supported so that there are only three unknown reactive elements at the supports. These can be determined by using the following fundamental equation of statics
explain: For a 2D structure, the three independent equations of equilibrium are the summation of horizontal forces, vertical forces, and moments about any point.

q: 16. An arch with three hinges, is a structure
explain: As established in Q. 250, the three hinges provide enough equations to solve for all reactions using statics alone.

q: 17. An arch may be subjected to
options: thrust, shear force and bending moment
explain: Unlike a funicular arch, a general arch structure under arbitrary loading must resist axial compression (thrust), transverse shear, and bending moments.

q: 18. If two forces acting at a joint are not along the straight line, then for the equilibrium of the joint
options: one of the forces must be zero
forces must be equal and of the same sign
forces must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign
explain: If only two non-collinear members meet at a joint with no external load, both must carry zero force to satisfy ΣH=0 and ΣV=0.

q: 19. The bending moment at a section tends to bend or deflect the beam and the internal stress resist its bending. The resistance offered by the internal stresses, to the bending, is called
explain: Bending stress (or flexural stress) is the internal resistance developed by the fibers of a beam to counteract the external bending moment.

q: 20. In a simple bending theory, one of the assumptions is that the material of the beam is isotropic. This assumption means that the
options: normal stress remains constant in all directions
normal stress varies linearly in the material
elastic constants are same in all the directions
elastic constants varies linearly in the material
explain: An isotropic material has identical physical and elastic properties (like Young's Modulus and Poisson's ratio) in all directions at any given point.

q: 21. The section modulus of a rectangular section about an axis through its C.G., is
explain: For a rectangle, I = bd³/12 and y_max = d/2. Thus, Z = (bd³/12) / (d/2) = bd²/6.

q: 22. The maximum shear stress developed in a beam of circular section is ............ the average shear stress.
explain: In a circular section, the maximum shear stress at the neutral axis is 4/3 (or 1.33) times the average shear stress.

q: 23. Longitudinal cracks observed in timber beams are due to
options: application of concentrated loads over the beams
timber not being strong in compression
explain: Timber is relatively weak in shear parallel to the grain. Horizontal shear stress causes the fibers to slide past each other, resulting in longitudinal cracks.

q: 24. The torsional rigidity of a shaft is given by ............
explain: Torsional rigidity is defined as the torque required to produce a unit radian of twist per unit length. From T/J = Gθ/L, GJ = TL/θ. Often represented as T/θ for a given length.

q: 25. The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam loaded with a UDL of w/m having span l is
explain: Standard formula: M_max = wl²/8 for a full-span UDL on a simply supported beam.

q: 26. Point of contraflexure is a point where bending moment
explain: At a point of contraflexure the bending moment passes through zero, changing from sagging to hogging (or vice versa).

q: 27. In case of a fixed beam loaded at its centre, the number of points at which BM is zero
explain: A centrally-loaded fixed beam has two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: 28. The maximum bending moment caused by a large number of equally spaced identical loads on a simply supported beam is (W=wL)
explain: As the number of equal point loads increases, the loading approaches a UDL, so max BM approaches WL/8.

q: 29. For a beam of uniform strength if its depth is maintained constant then its width will vary in proportion to
explain: As per the answer key for this set (uniform-strength beam with constant depth).

q: 30. Maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to concentrated load (w) at the mid point is
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/48EI for a central point load on a simply supported beam.

q: 31. The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying a concentrated load 'w' at the free end
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/3EI for a cantilever with a point load at the free end.

q: 32. The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying uniformly distributed load (w) over its span
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/8EI for a cantilever under UDL (W = total load = wL).

q: 33. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to uniformly distributed load (w) over the span is
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = 5WL³/384EI for UDL on a simply supported beam (W = total load = wL).

q: 34. Longitudinal cracks observed in timber beams are due to
options: application of concentrated loads over the beam
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: longitudinal splitting along the grain in timber is classically attributed to horizontal shear failure between layers — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: 35. The number of reaction components at a hinge on rollers support is
explain: A roller support provides only one reaction component, perpendicular to the rolling surface.

q: 36. A shear force diagram of a simply supported beam shows constant shear force throughout the span. It is subjected to
options: two concentrated loads spaced at points
explain: A pure applied couple (no other transverse loads) produces a constant shear force with a jump in the moment diagram, but constant SF throughout.

q: 37. The shear force on a beam and the displacement are related by
explain: As per the answer key; the standard beam relation is V = EI·d³y/dx³ (third derivative of deflection).
